[[Warnman language|Warnman]]? | iso3 = ant | glotto = anta1253 | glottorefname = Antakarinya | aiatsis = C5 | map2 = Lang Status 20-CR.svg | mapcaption2 = {{center|Antakarinya is classified as Critically Endangered by the [[UNESCO]] ''[[Atlas of the World's Languages in Danger]]''.}} }} '''Antakarinya''' (also Andagarinya, Antikirinya, Antikirrinya) is an [[Australian Aboriginal languages|Australian Aboriginal language]]. It is one of the [[Wati languages]] of the large [[Pama–Nyungan languages|Pama–Nyungan family]]. The [[Antakarinya people]] were greatly affected by the [[atomic testing]] at [[Maralinga]] in the 1950s and the language was similarly affected in an attempt to explain the tests.{{cite web|last=Fuss|first=Eloise|title=The Norwegian linguist and the Antikirrininya elder|url=http://www.abc.net.au/local/audio/2012/05/29/3513647.htm?site=northandwest|work=abc.net.au|publisher=Australian Broadcasting Commission|access-date=1 June 2012}} == Name == The name Antakarinya is almost certainly of [[Arandic languages|Arrandic]] origin. A probable etymology is ''antekerre'' ("south") and ''-nye'' (a suffix attached to directions or places indicating something from there).{{Cite book |last=Brown |first=Ingkama Bobby |url=https://books.google.com/books/about/Irrititja_the_Past.html?id=8YZGMwEACAAJ& |title=Irrititja - the Past: Antikirrinya History from Ingomar Station and Beyond |last2=Nœssan |first2=Petter Attila |date=2012 |publisher=Keeaira Press |isbn=978-0-9805942-5-6 |pages=13 |language=en}} [[Norman Tindale]] held the name means "westerners", from ''andakara'' ("west"). Wilkins & Petch (1997) states it is probably from [[Lower Arrernte language|Lower Arrernte]], from the words {{lang|axl|antekerre}} ("west") and {{lang|tsr|-arenye}} ("originating from"). == Further reading == * Ingkama Bobby Brown; Petter Attila Naessan, ''Irrititja – The Past: Antikirrinya History from Ingomar Station and Beyond'', Keeaira Press, 2012{{Cite book |last=Brown |first=Ingkama Bobby |url=https://books.google.com/books/about/Irrititja_the_Past.html?id=8YZGMwEACAAJ& |title=Irrititja - the Past: Antikirrinya History from Ingomar Station and Beyond |last2=Nœssan |first2=Petter Attila |date=2012 |publisher=Keeaira Press |isbn=978-0-9805942-5-6 |pages= |language=en}} ==References== {{Reflist}} {{Aboriginal South Australians}} [[Category:Critically endangered languages]] [[Category:Endangered indigenous Australian languages in South Australia]] {{ia-lang-stub}} [[Category:Western Desert language]]
